description: "Use when: creating or editing Markdown documentation, READMEs, or instructions"
applyTo: "**/*.md"

# Documentation 📚

Write docs to help people understand the project and get things done—not to show off how much we know. Keep them welcoming, useful and concise, especially for new developers.

## What belongs

- Document decisions and behavior that are implemented, tested and working.
- Explain important choices and their history when that context will help future readers.
- Keep TODOs out of user and developer guides. If a separate issue list is useful, organize it by priority and topic.

## Keep it tidy

- Check related docs before adding new material. Update outdated content and merge duplicates.
- Link to existing project or library docs instead of repeating them.
- Keep details close to the code unless they are useful in several places.
- Prefer practical links and simple steps over exhaustive technical references.

## Make it readable

- Use a warm, straightforward voice. A little humor and emojis are welcome when they make the guidance more enjoyable.
- Keep paragraphs short; split long explanations into smaller sections or lists.
- Follow [Markdown guidance](./markdown.instructions.md) for formatting and [Language guidance](./language.instructions.md) for inclusive wording and tone.
